description: Farmers Insurance Exchange offers home, life, business, and car insurance to American customers. It is one of the insurance providers that makes up the Farmers Insurance Group, along with Fire Insurance Exchange and Truck Insurance Exchange. Founded in 1928, the Farmers Insurance Group was created to provide insurance to farmers but has since expanded to offer its financial services to an array of customers. In 2020, the group announced that it would acquire financial service company MetLife Auto and Home.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: “What makes this organization such a great place to work is the emphasis on balancing personal and professional well-being,” says one Farmers Insurance employee. The nearly 100-year-old insurance company is moving into the future as it works with employees to establish new hybrid work schedules and provide more flexibility. Farmers has also committed to recruiting a more diverse workforce, recently forming the Enterprise Diversity and Inclusion Council to help the company reach its various D&I goals, including establishing implicit bias training for hiring managers and piloting referral programs to support more diverse applicant pools. The company also uses a Team Climate Assessment to make sure it’s responding to its employees the best it can to ensure a positive work climate.

“What makes this organization such a great place to work is the emphasis on balancing personal and professional well-being. My team was incredible when I had a family emergency earlier this year and it made all the difference to be able to focus on that so I could perform the best possible at my job.”

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Working parents have had an especially rough time during the pandemic. That’s why the insurer, based in Woodland Hills, Calif., worked to help its employees with children adjust over the past year. The firm expanded its resource group Parent Connect, offering webinars and tools to aid its working parents, while also developing a site on the company’s intranet to provide resources for children in school. One working parent at Farmers notes, “The flexibility, and understanding that I have four kids at home that now have to be essentially homeschooled and that my work schedule might have to change, was more than I could have ever expected.” The insurer also doled out over $91,000 in relief to employee families in need because of COVID-19, mostly from losing household income after layoffs.
